text: Upgrade cozo/git2 deps to clear audit advisories: RUSTSEC-2026-0041 lz4_flex via cozo chain, RUSTSEC-2026-0008 git2 0.19 unsound Buf deref

[SPIKE] Research and implement guardrails to prevent direct-to-main pushes by agents. Incident: commits cbbfb81 and 3fd285a were pushed directly to main bypassing branch protection after a PR merge. Research scope: (1) git pre-push hooks that block pushes to main locally, (2) GitHub branch protection hardening (require PR, disable admin bypass for agents), (3) agent-level instruction/checklist enforcement in copilot-instructions.md, (4) CI workflow to detect and alert on direct main commits. Deliverable: a recommendation with the lowest-friction approach that works for both human and agent contributors, plus implementation.

PDF document ingestion: add ability to parse and chunk PDF files of any size into the pipeline. Requires: PDF text extraction crate (evaluate pdf-extract, lopdf, pdfium), page/section-aware chunking strategy, handling of tables/images/figures (text extraction vs OCR), large-file streaming to avoid memory blowout, integration as a new parser backend alongside Markdown. Needs a spike to evaluate crate choices, extraction quality, and chunking strategy for structured documents.
Fix stale doc comment in src/chunk/mod.rs:5 — still references "LanceDB vectors to Kùzu graph nodes" but should reference CozoDB unified store

Persist embeddings in CozoDB HNSW index and implement semantic vector search (search_similar). Currently vectors are computed during sync but discarded. This is the primary value-add — enabling similarity-based documentation discovery beyond keyword matching. Planned internally as 009-F.

Expand MCP tool surface: add list_sources (enumerate indexed sources), get_chunk_by_id (retrieve chunk by SHA-256 ID), get_document (all chunks for a path), search_semantic (vector search, depends on HNSW), get_status (DB stats/health). Currently only search_local_docs and traverse_doc_links exist.

Wire incremental sync (sync_source) into the CLI sync command. The sync module exists and is tested (git diff + mtime diff + surgical re-ingestion) but cmd_sync uses the full pipeline::run instead. Add --full flag for existing behavior, make incremental the default.

Web crawler acquisition source: add type: url source to sources.yaml for crawling live documentation sites (e.g. learn.microsoft.com/azure/cosmos-db/). Requires: HTTP client (reqwest), HTML-to-Markdown converter, recursive link follower with configurable depth/domain limits, rate limiting, robots.txt compliance, deduplication. This is a new acquisition backend alongside git and local — follows the same pipeline interface (returns list of Markdown files for parse stage). Needs a spike first to evaluate crate choices and crawl strategy.

Word document (.docx) ingestion: add ability to parse and chunk Word documents of any size into the pipeline. Requires: OOXML parser crate (evaluate docx-rs, office-crypto, or zip + xml manual parsing), paragraph/heading-aware chunking, table extraction, embedded image handling, large-file streaming, integration as a new parser backend alongside Markdown and PDF. Needs a spike to evaluate crate choices, extraction fidelity, and chunking strategy for Word's nested structure.

E2E smoke test: configure sources.yaml with azure-cosmos-db-docs repo, run graphtor-docs sync, verify chunks loaded with graphtor-docs status, start MCP server with graphtor-docs serve, test search_local_docs and traverse_doc_links against real Cosmos DB documentation content.

Agent harness learning: Stage agent MUST NOT call backlogit_ship_shipment, backlogit_claim_shipment, backlogit_archive_item, or backlogit_delete_item. Stage only assembles shipments and gates readiness (verifies tasks are decomposed, plans reviewed, tests defined). Ship agent owns: claiming the shipment, feature branch creation, build loop, PR lifecycle, CI validation, review handling, operator-approved merge, and THEN backlogit_ship_shipment. Stage's terminal action is confirming readiness and reporting to the operator for Ship orchestration.

Mature the documentation source registry (sources.yaml) to support mixed-format ingestion per source: each Git, URL, or local source entry should declare which document types it contains (PDF, DOCX, Markdown) so the pipeline dispatches the correct parser per file. Add schema validation, default format lists, and per-source format override configuration. This enables a single Git repo source to ingest its Markdown, PDF, and DOCX files in one pass.

Fully test PDF, DOCX, and Git repo documentation ingestion: create comprehensive integration tests covering each acquisition source type end-to-end (acquire → parse → chunk → embed → load). Validate correct handling of edge cases (large files, malformed input, empty documents, nested structures) for each format. Ensure deterministic chunk IDs and idempotent re-ingestion across all three source types.

Streaming PDF parser with heading-aware chunk accumulation: Replace current whole-file PDF parsing with page-streaming via lopdf (random page access). Stream pages one at a time, detect heading boundaries via font-size heuristics, accumulate text into section buffers, and emit chunks at semantic boundaries rather than arbitrary page breaks. This bounds memory usage (one section at a time vs. entire PDF), produces semantically meaningful chunks aligned to document structure, avoids near-duplicate chunks from overlapping page windows, and naturally fits the existing doc_chunks schema (headings, content, position). Requires evaluating lopdf vs pdf-extract for font metadata access. Current pdf-extract approach loads entire PDF and produces flat text with no heading detection — debug-mode processing of a 109MB PDF takes 45+ minutes.

PDFium-render dual backend for large PDF ingestion: Replace pdf-extract with pdfium-render for PDFs ≥20 MiB. PDFium opens documents lazily (instant for any size) vs pdf-extract's lopdf which eagerly parses all xref entries serially (>20 min for 104 MB). Implementation: PdfiumBackend struct with try_parse() fallback pattern, DLL discovery via env var → exe dir → system path. Already benchmarked: pdf-extract DNF on Cosmos DB PDF, pdfium-render expected <10s. Dependency: pdfium-render 0.9.1 (thread_safe, pdfium_latest features). Feature branch exists: feat/pdfium-large-pdf-backend with partial implementation.

Comprehensive documentation for all aspects of graphtor-docs: architecture overview, data pipeline stages (acquire/parse/embed/load), MCP tool reference, configuration guide (sources.yaml schema, all source types), CLI command reference, developer setup guide, embedding model details (all-MiniLM-L6-v2 via Candle), CozoDB schema and query patterns, incremental sync design, and troubleshooting guide. Should cover both user-facing (how to configure and run) and developer-facing (how to contribute and extend) perspectives. Output: docs/ directory with well-structured markdown files.

Refactor PdfExtractBackend Pass 2 to use output_doc_page in a page-by-page loop instead of output_doc (full traversal), enabling heading-aware chunking for PDFs of any size. Currently the 20 MiB LARGE_PDF_THRESHOLD guard forces all large PDFs into page-based chunking with heading_hierarchy: ["Page N"]. The histogram (Pass 1) is already bounded at 30 pages and is not the bottleneck — Pass 2 is. Switching Pass 2 to output_doc_page makes the threshold guard unnecessary and restores section-based chunk IDs for large PDFs. Analysis: docs/research/pdf-pass2-page-by-page-refactor-2026-05-04.md

Rebrand MCP tool names to be source-agnostic: rename `search_ms_docs_semantic` → `search_semantic`, ensure tool descriptions don't imply MS-only scope. The underlying engine already handles any Markdown source — the naming is the only barrier to multi-workspace adoption.

Add pre-sync commands to start.ps1: run `graphtor-docs sync` and `backlogit sync` before launching copilot. Ensures both the doc index and backlog index are fresh at session start without relying on the agent or operator to remember. Complements the auto-sync-on-serve feature but works immediately without code changes to graphtor itself.

Workspace auto-discovery mode: graphtor automatically detects and indexes .md files in the current repo without requiring manual sources.yaml configuration. Enables zero-config adoption in any workspace — just run `graphtor-docs install && graphtor-docs sync` and it indexes the local repo's docs.

Auto-sync on MCP server start: when `graphtor-docs serve` launches the MCP server, it should detect stale or unsynced content (via commit hash / mtime comparison) and perform an incremental sync before accepting tool calls. Eliminates the manual `sync` step — the agent gets fresh data the moment it connects. Should be non-blocking (serve immediately, sync in background) with a status tool indicating sync progress.

Add composite MCP tool `research_topic` that wraps the common search→traverse→retrieve workflow into a single tool call. Keeps individual tools intact but provides a one-shot convenience for the 80% case: (1) search_local_docs or search_semantic based on query, (2) auto-traverse top_k results 1-2 hops, (3) deduplicate, (4) return enriched results with full content + related context. Reduces 4-6 round-trips to 1 for the typical agent research pattern.

Add `--json` flag to every CLI command that outputs results in JSON-RPC 2.0 format (matching MCP server response structure) so agents can consume CLI output identically to MCP tool responses. Also add a `graphtor-docs manifest` command that emits a JSON-RPC 2.0 tool manifest listing all CLI commands with names, descriptions, and parameter schemas — mirroring what the MCP server returns via `tools/list` on initialization. This enables CLI-first agent workflows without requiring the MCP STDIO server, and ensures parity between CLI and MCP surfaces.

Update project documentation (README.md, AGENTS.md, docs/) to incorporate latest feature additions: --json global flag for JSON-RPC 2.0 CLI output, manifest subcommand, zero-config workspace adoption (init/install/doctor/upgrade/uninstall), and docs rebranding from LocalDocRAG to graphtor-docs. Ensure usage examples, architecture references, and CLI command listings reflect the current tool surface.

Replace brute-force O(n) vector search with CozoDB native HNSW index for sub-logarithmic approximate nearest-neighbor lookup. Current implementation loads all embeddings from doc_vectors as JSON strings, deserializes, computes cosine similarity in Rust, and sorts — O(n) per query. HNSW would provide O(log n) search, eliminate JSON serde overhead, and enable scaling to the full 703-repo MS Docs corpus (500k+ chunks). Requires schema v3 migration, native vector column type, and re-ingestion pass.

Installation of graphtor seems to install the MCP server configuration in .github/copilot/mcp.json, which is absolutely not correct as it is not recognized by VS Code, Copilot CLI, or any other IDE or CLI.
telemetry output for backlogit metrics reporting
pre-warm indexing/sync with operator-friendly progress reporting

graphtor needs a way to be called in a pre-warm manner to fully index/sync the workspace database before starting copilot. Currently, calling sync outputs a lot of graph related syntax to the terminal, which doesn't mean much to the operator. Instead, graphtor needs to assess total amount of content it needs to ingest and show either a progress bar in the terminal or a stream of output showing the file being ingested and the percentage to total completion at the individual file level and at the total volume of content to ingest level.
Add telemetry to output to be used by backlogit for metrics reporting.
multi-database file support

As part of multi-database file support, allow sources.yaml to specify the target database filename for a source group so content can be routed into a specific database file such as powerbi.db or rust-docs.db.

Stash this: multi-database file support: Consider this: you want to be able to support multiple database files within Graphtor-docs so that you can have one for Rust, another one for C Sharp, and another one for Power BI to house all of your documentation that you need. You want to support that one content source or type and then be able to reuse that across multiple projects so that you don't have to re-ingest the data for every project using those sources.
